task: Fix a regression in commit 91a7f49fa that broke workflow thought persistence via a callback retention bug and a duplicate event-adapter finalize causing ThoughtConsumer IntegrityError.

key_reasoning.reason: Three distinct components — AgentStreamingCallback (callback layer), LangGraphEventAdapter (agent/event-adapter layer), ThoughtConsumer (persistence layer) — across 3 architectural areas, with the base model's existing merge-based update() as a candidate shared utility the fix may need to adopt.

Root cause is precisely diagnosed down to file:line by prior investigation, but the technical analysis explicitly defers the fix-layer decision to spec stage ('candidate fix layers... to be evaluated/decided'), and the existing test test_error_handling_during_save asserts the opposite of what a consumer-side fix would need — an unresolved design decision with rework risk.

No exact precedent for the combined fix; the retain bug is on the default/common code path (SWITCHYARD_ENABLED=False) affecting essentially all non-Switchyard workflow executions; the consumer thread pool silently swallows exceptions (unobserved Future); and the supervisor vs non-supervisor event-adapter paths are asymmetric, risking an incomplete fix.

~3 source files (agent_streaming_callback.py, langgraph_event_adapter.py, thought_consumer.py) plus 3 companion test files needing updates/new cases, spanning 3+ directories (agents/callbacks, agents, service/workflow_execution and their mirrored test dirs); a new integration-level regression test may also be needed since no end-to-end ThoughtQueue→ThoughtConsumer→get_root() test exists.

red_flags_applied: Requirements Clarity bumped from M to L: the technical analysis frames the fix-layer choice as explicitly undecided ('to be evaluated/decided at spec stage'), matching the TBD/deferred-decision red flag.
